items.title: Sustained improvement in sickle cell cardiomyopathy after haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is superior to that with disease-modifying therapy.
items.abstract: Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is curative for sickle cell disease (SCD) - a group of inherited haemoglobin disorders encompassing homozygous haemoglobin S (HbSS) and compound heterozygous sickling disorders, including haemoglobin SC disease (HbSC), haemoglobin S/β 0 -thalassaemia (HbSβ 0 ), haemoglobin S/β + -thalassaemia (HbSβ + ), etc., but its long-term impact on SCD myocardial remodelling is incompletely characterized. We performed serial cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) and echocardiography in children and young adults with SCD undergoing matched-sibling or haploidentical HSCT in a prospective clinical trial with up to 36 months of post-HSCT follow-up. CMR assessments were conducted before HSCT and through the post-HSCT period. Echocardiographic parameters at 12 months post HSCT were compared with those of age-matched participants receiving disease-modifying therapies (DMTs). Among 20 HSCT recipients (mean age 14.8 years), CMR demonstrated progressive reductions in biventricular volumes and left atrial volume over 36 months, with preservation of ejection fraction. Extra-cellular volume, a surrogate marker of myocardial fibrosis, showed significant improvement from baseline, having normalized in nearly all participants assessed at 36 months. Compared with age-matched DMT recipients, HSCT recipients had lower tricuspid regurgitant jet velocity and improved diastolic parameters at 12 months post-HSCT, with normalization of cardiac output on echocardiography. These findings demonstrate sustained reversal of myocardial fibrosis and structural cardiac remodelling after HSCT for SCD. HSCT may, therefore, modify the trajectory of SCD cardiomyopathy beyond the improvements achieved with current DMTs.

items.title: Reduced Adverse Events Without Survival Benefit With HeartMate 3 vs. HeartMate II in Japan.
items.abstract: HeartMate 3 (Abbott Laboratories), a fully magnetically levitated left ventricular assist device (LVAD), has shown improved hemocompatibility vs. previous devices, but nationwide real-world data in Japan remain limited. Using the Japanese nationwide registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support (J-MACS), we analyzed patients who underwent de novo implantation of HeartMate 3 or HeartMate II between 2013 and 2025. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, stroke, and device dysfunction requiring exchange or explantation within 2 years. In all, 978 patients were included in the study (HeartMate 3, n=486; HeartMate II, n=492). The 2-year cumulative incidence of the primary outcome was significantly lower in the HeartMate 3 group than in the HeartMate II group (9% vs. 23%; P<0.001). HeartMate 3 was independently associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 0.35; 95% confidence interval 0.23-0.51; P<0.001), which remained consistent in competing-risk and several statistically matched analyses. The incidence of hemocompatibility-related adverse events, including major bleeding, stroke, and device dysfunction, was significantly lower in the HeartMate 3 group. In contrast, 2- and 5-year overall mortality did not differ significantly between groups (<10% for both devices). In this nationwide Japanese registry, HeartMate 3 reduced major LVAD-related complications without improving survival, supporting its clinical advantages in contemporary LVAD management.
items.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society

items.title: A Familial Case of Thauvin-Robinet-Faivre Syndrome (TROFAS), Presenting With Postaxial Polydactyly and Upper Lip Vascular Malformation.
items.abstract: Thauvin-Robinet-Faivre syndrome (TROFAS, OMIM #617107) is a recently identified autosomal recessive disorder characterised by syndromic overgrowth, facial dysmorphism, mild intellectual disability, variable congenital anomalies, and occasional tumour occurrence. TROFAS results from homozygous or compound heterozygous variants in the FIBP gene, encoding the intracellular binding protein for acidic fibroblast growth factor. This protein plays a role in the fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signalling pathway, which is involved in cell proliferation and contributes to the development of several structures, such as the nervous system, optic vesicles, and blood vessels. Prior to the present report, TROFAS has been described in 10 patients from seven families, four of which are of Turkish origin. We report two additional Turkish siblings from a previously unreported family harbouring the recurrent homozygous c.412-3_415dupCAGTTTG likely pathogenic variant in FIBP. Both presented with typical TROFAS features; however, the male sibling exhibited a more severe neurodevelopmental profile and additional malformations, including postaxial polydactyly and upper lip vascular malformation, which, to our knowledge, have not previously been reported in association with TROFAS. A detailed clinical characterisation of these two new cases contributes to a more comprehensive delineation of the syndrome, adding potentially novel phenotypic features requiring confirmation in additional patients.

items.title: Long-term Nlrp3 gain-of-function mutation promotes cardiac dysfunction independent of inflammasome in mice.
items.abstract: Cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome (CAPS) is an autoinflammatory disease caused by gain-of-function mutations in human nucleotide-binding domain, leucine-rich repeat-containing protein 3 (NLRP3), which lead to constitutive inflammasome activation and excessive IL-1β secretion. Long-term IL-1 blockade has markedly improved patient outcomes by preventing systemic inflammation and amyloidosis. However, whether chronic NLRP3 mutation exerts inflammasome-independent effects on the cardiac function remains unknown. We generated Nlrp3C257Y/WT knock-in mice as a novel CAPS model. Long-term survival, systemic inflammation, and cardiac function were assessed by biochemical, histological, and echocardiographic analyses. To determine inflammasome dependency, Nlrp3C257Y/WT mice were crossed with Asc-/- mice to generate double-mutant Nlrp3C257Y/WT × Asc-/- offspring. Nlrp3C257Y/WT mice exhibited early-onset cutaneous inflammation that gradually subsided, these mice developed marked left ventricular (LV) dilatation and mild systolic dysfunction after approximately 6 mo of age. Histological analysis revealed interstitial myocardial fibrosis in Nlrp3C257Y/WT mice. This result indicates that Nlrp3C257Y/WT mutation, which operates as a gain-of-function variant for inflammasome activation, impairs cardiac function largely driven by an inflammasome-dependent mechanism. In contrast, Nlrp3C257Y/WT × Asc-/- mice exhibited marked resolution of systemic inflammation; nevertheless, LV dilatation and reduced fractional shortening persisted. Long-term Nlrp3C257Y/WT mutation can lead to persistent cardiac dysfunction not only through inflammasome activation but also via inflammasome-independent mechanisms. Our findings reveal previously unrecognized inflammasome-independent mechanisms linking NLRP3 signaling to cardiac dysfunction. This study expands knowledge of the pathophysiological spectrum of CAPS and highlights inflammasome-independent NLRP3 signaling as a potential therapeutic target to prevent chronic cardiac complications in patients with CAPS and NLRP3-associated disorders.

items.title: Information quality, understandability, actionability and readability of large language models for HIV health education: A cross-platform evaluation.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate health education materials, but their suitability for patient-facing human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) education remains insufficiently evaluated. We assessed the information quality, understandability, actionability, readability, text structure and source transparency of HIV patient education materials generated by six LLMs or artificial intelligence platforms. In this cross-sectional study, 100 common HIV patient education questions across 10 domains were submitted once in English to ChatGPT 5.4-Thinking, DeepSeek-V3.2, Doubao, ERNIE Bot 5.0 Preview, Ant Afu and Gemini 3.1 Pro, yielding 600 responses. Responses were evaluated using Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials (PEMAT-P), EQ IP-36, DISCERN, Global Quality Score (GQS), artificial intelligence response quality metric (AIRM), Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmarks and seven readability indices. Platform comparisons used paired Friedman tests with Wilcoxon-Holm post hoc analyses; topic analyses used question-level aggregation followed by Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn-Holm comparisons. Significant family-adjusted differences were observed across platforms for all prespecified text-structure, quality/understandability/actionability and readability outcomes. At the topic level, five of six text-structure outcomes, PEMAT-P Understandability, PEMAT-P Actionability, the exploratory PEMAT-P composite score and all seven readability indices differed significantly after family adjustment, whereas EQ IP-36, DISCERN, GQS, AIRM and JAMA did not. Overall actionability was limited and readability demands were high. LLM-generated HIV patient education materials showed substantial cross-platform and topic-level heterogeneity. These findings support the use of LLMs as expert-reviewed drafting tools rather than independent patient education sources. Direct factual accuracy, guideline concordance, hallucination and clinical safety were not assessed.

items.title: [Research progress and vaccination strategies of respiratory syncytial virus vaccines for pregnant women].
items.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a predominant global pathogen responsible for severe lower respiratory tract infections and hospitalizations in infants, especially those aged under six months. To date, no vaccines have been approved for active immunization against RSV in infant populations, leaving monoclonal antibodies as the primary modality for immediate, direct RSV protection. Maternal vaccination during pregnancy has evolved as a critical passive immunization approach, wherein vaccine-elicited maternal antibodies cross the placenta to confer early-life protection on neonates and young infants. This review elaborates on the pathogenesis of RSV infection and the features of host immune responses to RSV, summarizes key advances and remaining bottlenecks in RSV vaccine development, and focuses on evaluating the efficacy, safety, and immunogenicity of the prefusion F protein-based RSV vaccine (RSVpreF) based on latest clinical trial findings and post-marketing surveillance data. Additionally, it compares RSV vaccination guidelines and strategic recommendations issued by major global health authorities, including the World Health Organization (WHO) and the European Medicines Agency (EMA). This article further discusses persistent challenges and prospective research priorities in this field, covering public awareness of RSV vaccination, global vaccine accessibility, long-term safety profile monitoring, and vaccine applicability in special populations. Collectively, this review aims to provide evidence-based references to guide clinical practice and optimize public health decision-making regarding RSV prevention. 呼吸道合胞病毒（RSV）是导致全球0~1岁婴幼儿，特别是6月龄以下婴幼儿，严重下呼吸道感染及住院的主要病原体。目前尚无获批用于婴幼儿主动免疫的RSV疫苗，仅能通过单克隆抗体为婴幼儿提供保护。因此，通过给妊娠期孕妇接种RSV疫苗，诱导其体内产生抗体并经胎盘转运至胎儿，成为婴儿早期提供被动免疫的重要预防策略。本综述阐述了RSV的发病机制与免疫应答特点，梳理疫苗研发历程中的关键突破与难点，重点基于最新临床试验与上市后监测数据，分析妊娠期接种呼吸道合胞病毒融合前F蛋白疫苗（RSVpreF）的有效性、安全性及免疫原性证据。同时，本文综述对比了世界卫生组织、欧洲药品管理局等主要卫生机构的接种建议与策略差异，并深入探讨了在疫苗认知、全球可及性、长期安全性证据及特殊人群应用等方面面临的挑战与未来研究方向，旨在为临床实践与公共卫生决策提供循证参考。.
items.journal: Zhonghua yu fang yi xue za zhi [Chinese journal of preventive medicine]

items.title: Talquetamab and Its Effect on Relapsed and Refractory Multiple Myeloma.
items.abstract: Relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) remains a challenging condition despite many advances in immunotherapies. Outcomes are particularly dismal in patients who are refractory to these three major classes of proteasome inhibitors, immunomodulatory drugs, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapies. Novel bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) have shown some promising efficacy in heavily pretreated patients, even those with triple- and penta-refractory disease. Talquetamab is a BsAb recently approved for the treatment of relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma. Talquetamab demonstrated a high overall response rate of approximately 70%, including in patients that are previously treated with T-cell therapies. The safety profile of talquetamab is consistent with other BsAbs, with similar adverse events. The efficacy of talquetamab and other therapies, including CAR-T cell treatments, remains an area of active research, as resistance to anti-B-cell maturation antigen therapies poses a clinical challenge. Current trials are exploring the use of talquetamab in combination therapies. There is now adequate data to further support talquetamab's efficacy, making it a very important addition to the RRMM treatment domain. Résumé Le myélome multiple récidivant et réfractaire (MMRR) reste une maladie difficile malgré les nombreux progrès des immunothérapies. Les résultats sont particulièrement sombres chez les patients réfractaires à ces trois grandes classes d’inhibiteurs du protéasome, de médicaments immunomodulateurs, d’anticorps monoclonaux (AcM) et de thérapies par lymphocytes T à récepteurs d’antigènes chimériques (CAR). De nouveaux anticorps bispécifiques (BsAbs) ont montré une efficacité prometteuse chez les patients lourdement prétraités, même ceux atteints d’une maladie triple et penta réfractaire. Le talquetamab est un BsAb récemment approuvé pour le traitement du myélome multiple récidivant et réfractaire. Le talquetamab a démontré un taux de réponse global élevé d’environ 70 %, y compris chez les patients préalablement traités par thérapies par lymphocytes T. Le profil d’innocuité du talquetamab est conforme à celui d’autres BsAb, avec des événements indésirables similaires. L’efficacité du talquetamab et d’autres thérapies, y compris les traitements par cellules CAR‐T, reste un domaine de recherche actif, car la résistance aux thérapies antigéniques de maturation des cellules B pose un défi clinique. Les essais en cours explorent l’utilisation du talquetamab dans des thérapies combinées. Il existe désormais des données adéquates pour étayer davantage l’efficacité du talquetamab, ce qui en fait un ajout très important au domaine de traitement RRMM.

items.title: Neuro-Immune Interactions in the Tumour Microenvironment: Implications for Cancer Progression and Treatment.
items.abstract: The nervous and immune systems, once viewed as distinct biological networks, are now understood to be closely linked in regulating cancer development, progression, and responses to therapy. Neural structures infiltrate the tumour microenvironment and communicate with immune cells, influencing key processes such as tumour growth, invasion, and metastatic spread. Through neurotransmitters, neuropeptides, and continuous signalling between peripheral tissues and the brain, nerves affect immune cell recruitment, activity, and overall immune balance. Factors including psychological stress, circadian rhythm disturbances, and gut-brain communication further shape antitumour immune responses, highlighting the complexity of these interactions. Research suggests that neuronal signalling not only contributes to cancer-associated symptoms, such as pain, but also affects the efficacy of chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy. Neural biomarkers may provide prognostic value, while interventions targeting neural pathways could strengthen anticancer immunity. Nevertheless, major challenges remain, including cellular heterogeneity, dynamic spatial and temporal interactions, and the limitations of existing experimental models. Continued progress in molecular techniques, bioinformatics, and cross-disciplinary research will be crucial for clarifying these mechanisms. Investigating the neuro-immune-cancer interface offers significant potential for developing innovative treatment approaches that combine neuroscience, immunology, and oncology to enhance patient survival and quality of life.

items.title: Dose Optimization of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Policy opportunity to reduce costs and improve access to immunotherapy in the United States.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized cancer treatment, but are associated with high costs and limited accessibility. Optimizing dosing strategy to achieve a Pharmacokinetics/Pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) supported alternative lower dose (PPALD) that maintains clinical benefit and offers a cost-minimization strategy with substantial health system savings. We conducted a literature review of Phase 1/2 trials describing the PPALD dose of three commonly used ICIs: Pembrolizumab, Nivolumab and Atezolizumab. Alternate dosing strategies based on data for pembrolizumab (2mg/kg), nivolumab (2mg/kg) and atezolizumab (10mg/kg) were proposed. Public CMS Medicare Part B data on expenditure for these therapies was used to obtain average cost/dose, mg/dose, and number of Medicare beneficiaries between 2018-2021. Costs were calculated based on current FDA approved dosing and alternate dosing strategies. PPALD resulted in substantially lower drug costs per patient for an 80kg individual compared with fixed dosing: pembrolizumab ($7,393.60 vs $9,242.00), nivolumab ($4,153.60 vs $12,460.80), and atezolizumab ($5,744.00 vs $8,616.00). Estimated 2018-2021 Medicare savings based on beneficiaries were $382.2 million for pembrolizumab, $943.1 million for nivolumab, and $114.4 million for atezolizumab, totaling nearly $1.44 billion. Alternate immunotherapy dosing represents a high-value cost saving strategy to reduce health care costs and improve global access. Implementation requires regulatory adaptation, smaller vials, or vial-sharing to minimize waste. This policy analysis demonstrates that evidence-based alternate dosing of commonly used checkpoint inhibitors (Pembrolizumab, Nivolumab and Atezolizumab) could substantially reduce drug expenses while maintaining efficacy. Using Medicare Part B utilization data, we estimated that implementation of these alternative dosing strategies can help save over $1.44 billion between 2018-2021. These findings have important implications for health policy by improving patient access to immunotherapy and curtailing financial toxicity. This can be further facilitated by the support of policymakers, regulatory agencies supporting prospective validation studies and development of reimbursement models that encourage dose optimization.

items.title: Tumor endothelial cells as vascular immune gatekeepers: reprogramming the vascular-immune interface for cancer immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Despite durable clinical responses to immunotherapy in a subset of patients, most solid tumors remain refractory owing to an immune-excluded phenotype characterized by limited trafficking, infiltration, and function of effector immune cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Tumor endothelial cells (TECs) function as vascular immune gatekeepers that orchestrate this process. Driven by persistent pro-angiogenic signaling and metabolic stress, TECs establish a multilayered immune barrier through structurally abnormal, poorly perfused vasculature, endothelial anergy, and active immunosuppressive programs. TECs directly suppress effector T-cell and natural killer (NK)-cell function through checkpoint-like ligands, death-ligand pathways, and immunometabolic mechanisms involving adenosine production and tryptophan catabolism. Simultaneously, they recruit, retain, and reprogram immunosuppressive leukocytes, thereby reinforcing immune exclusion and therapeutic resistance. Here, we propose a TEC-centric vascular immune gatekeeping framework and review strategies to reprogram tumor vessels from immune barriers into conduits for effective immune-cell trafficking and activation. We discuss endothelial-directed monotherapies that transiently normalize or reset TEC states, together with combination strategies integrating vascular modulation with immune checkpoint blockade, adoptive and innate immune-cell therapies, cancer vaccines, oncolytic viruses, STING agonists, and multifunctional antibodies. We also highlight key translational considerations, including biomarker-guided patient stratification, pharmacodynamic monitoring using mechanism-based endpoints, and optimization of treatment dose and scheduling within the vascular normalization window. Overall, this review establishes endothelial reprogramming as a central strategy for overcoming vascular immune gatekeeping and provides a mechanistic framework for biomarker-guided vascular-immune combination therapies in solid tumors.

items.title: Sociocultural Determinants of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Prevention Behaviors Among Non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic Adults in the United States.
items.abstract: Prevention is critical to reduce hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) burden, however, sociocultural influences on engagement in HCC preventive behaviors among populations at elevated risk are rarely examined together. We sought to evaluate sociocultural factors associated with HCC preventive behaviors among Non-Hispanic Black (NHB) and Hispanic adults. Pooled 2015-2024 NHIS data were used to identify NHB and Hispanic adults. HCC prevention behaviors included hepatitis B (HBV) vaccination, hepatitis C (HCV) testing, alcohol risk reduction, healthy weight, and physical activity. Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated associations between sociocultural factors and prevention behaviors adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, healthcare access, and immigration factors. Among 74,162 adults (NHB: 44.7%, n=33,166; Hispanic: 55.3%, n=40,996), HBV vaccination was lower among individuals aged 45-64 compared with those aged 18-30 years old (aOR 0.38; 95%CI 0.34-0.42), whereas college graduates had higher vaccine uptake (aOR 2.01; 95%CI 1.70-2.38). Adults aged 31-44 years were more likely to get tested for HCV (aOR 1.88; 95%CI 1.57-2.26). Alcohol moderation was higher among women (aOR 2.01; 95%CI 1.81-2.22) and lower among Hispanic than NHB adults (aOR 0.53; 95%CI 0.46-0.60). Higher education attainment was associated with healthy weight (aOR 1.56; 95%CI 1.38-1.77). Immigration status modified racial/ethnic prevention patterns (interaction p=0.009); long-term foreign-born noncitizen Black adults had higher vaccination rates (aOR 3.50; 95%CI 1.37-8.94). Engagement in HCC prevention behaviors among NHB and Hispanic adults was strongly affected by age, education, insurance coverage, healthcare access, and immigration context, highlighting structural influences on prevention opportunities. Equity-focused strategies expanding vaccination, screening, and lifestyle interventions are required.
items.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal surgery : official journal of the Society for Surgery of the Alimentary Tract

items.title: Multifactorial Contributors to Diagnostic Delay in a High-Risk Patient with Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Case Report with Clinical Lessons.
items.abstract: Patients at high risk for primary liver cancer (PLC) are recommended to undergo PLC surveillance at least every six months. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is a commonly used biomarker; however, approximately 15-30% of PLC cases remain AFP-negative throughout their course. Therefore, surveillance in high-risk populations should be based on liver imaging. Any newly detected or progressive lesion should be further characterized by contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), or contrast-enhanced ultrasound, following guideline-based classification and follow-up recommendations. This case details a 45-year-old Chinese male with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and a family history of PLC. As a high-risk individual for PLC, he did not undergo regular PLC surveillance for three years. During opportunistic encounters for acute myocardial infarction and abdominal pain, the attending specialists failed to appreciate the progression of liver imaging findings. In addition, the COVID-19 pandemic may have further aggravated pre-existing difficulties with follow-up and access to care, contributing to a delayed diagnosis of PLC. This case illustrates how a combination of physician-related, patient-related, and social-environmental factors contributed to surveillance failure and diagnostic delay in a high-risk patient with PLC. It reflects on why guideline-recommended interventions were not implemented at each healthcare encounter, how to correctly interpret AFP, and how to improve adherence to surveillance among high-risk populations for PLC. The insights from this case aim to inform systematic improvements in PLC monitoring for patients with chronic HBV infection.

items.title: The ncRNA-Epigenetic-Cuproptosis Axis in Liver Diseases: From Copper Homeostasis to Precision Hepatology.
items.abstract: Cuproptosis, a recently defined copper-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by excess intracellular copper, is characterized by copper binding to lipoylated tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle proteins, causing aberrant protein oligomerization, iron-sulfur cluster loss, and proteotoxic stress. Given the liver's central role in copper homeostasis, hepatocytes are particularly vulnerable to this death modality. This review examines the emerging non-coding RNA (ncRNA)-epigenetic-cuproptosis axis in liver diseases, critically evaluating the evidence across a spectrum from well-established biochemical principles to largely hypothetical connections. Epigenetic mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, and N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modifications, can modulate cuproptosis sensitivity. The methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3)-m6A- fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMR1)-ferredoxin 1 (FDX1) axis, which confers cuproptosis resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through translational repression of FDX1, represents the strongest mechanistic evidence in hepatic contexts. ncRNAs, including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and circular RNAs (circRNAs), add additional regulatory layers; miR-133a-5p has been shown to facilitate cuproptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma by targeting ATP7B. We additionally highlight high-copper HCC phenotypes, the MYC-CTR1 and COMMD3 pro-tumor axes, and ferroptosis-cuproptosis combination strategies as priority translational directions. We systematically evaluate the ncRNA-epigenetic-cuproptosis axis across major liver diseases, including metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease, alcohol-associated liver disease, viral hepatitis, cholestatic liver disease, hepatic fibrosis, ischemia-reperfusion injury, Wilson disease, and HCC. Evidence tiers range from direct functional validation, such as copper ionophore-induced cuproptosis in HCC cells and cholestatic liver injury models, through promising but incomplete data, to largely bioinformatic associations lacking functional validation. Translational opportunities include biomarker development, copper ionophore-based therapeutics, and ncRNA-targeted interventions; we further distinguish mechanistic evidence from available human clinical data and outline how tumor copper phenotype, ncRNA signatures, viral etiology, immune context, and individual copper metabolism status could inform precision hepatology. We identify six priority questions and propose a research roadmap to advance this field from correlative associations toward rigorous mechanistic understanding, quantification of cuproptosis relative to established liver-cell death pathways, and eventual clinical implementation in precision hepatology.
items.journal: Journal of clinical and experimental hepatology

items.title: Multifocal intracranial aneurysms and a clinical diagnosis of ruptured retinal arterial macroaneurysm in presumed hepatitis B-associated polyarteritis nodosa: A case report.
items.abstract: Polyarteritis nodosa (PAN) is a necrotizing medium-artery vasculitis; intracranial aneurysms are rare. A woman in her early thirties with hypertension and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positivity presented with thunderclap headache, vomiting, and blurred vision. Available records described intracranial hemorrhage associated with a right posterior cerebral artery (PCA) aneurysm, but the index computed tomography/angiography images and full report were unavailable to classify the hemorrhage. The aneurysm was coil embolized with intentional parent-vessel sacrifice. Subsequent magnetic resonance imaging showed right occipitotemporal and thalamic infarction with hemorrhagic transformation-an expected consequence of right PCA sacrifice. A small acute left caudate infarct outside the treated territory raised a separate multifocal or embolic mechanism. Time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography showed the partially occluded right P2p/P3 PCA aneurysm and 2 distal left internal carotid artery aneurysms. During the same admission, subhyaloid and intraretinal hemorrhage led to a clinical diagnosis of ruptured retinal arterial macroaneurysm; no fundus photograph, fluorescein angiogram, or optical coherence tomography angiography was available, and follow-up structural optical coherence tomography did not show the lesion. Elevated inflammatory markers, neuropathic symptoms, multifocal aneurysms, and HBsAg positivity led rheumatology to a working diagnosis of HBV-associated PAN. Because no biopsy or visceral angiography was performed and accepted classification criteria were not securely met, the diagnosis is described as presumed. The teaching point is attribution: the dominant stroke was iatrogenic; the contralateral infarct and multifocal aneurysms prompted systemic evaluation; ocular hemorrhage may be a clue but does not establish shared vasculitic causation.

items.title: Burden, healthcare utilization, and costs of chronic liver disease-related hospitalizations in California: a population-based study of trends and projections, 2005-2035.
items.abstract: Long-term trends in hospitalization burden, healthcare utilization, and costs of chronic liver disease (CLD) in the United States remain poorly characterized. Using statewide hospital discharge data, we quantified trends from 2005 to 2018 and projected future burden through 2035 across demographic subgroups. We used average annual percent change (AAPC) to quantify trends in hospitalized patients, hospitalizations, deaths, along with age-standardized rates (ASHPR, ASHR, and ASMR); hospitalizations per patient-year, average length of stay, 30-day readmission, in-hospital mortality; and inflation-adjusted hospital charges (2019 US dollars). Analyses were conducted overall and for hepatitis B virus(HBV), hepatitis C virus(HCV), alcohol-associated liver disease(ALD), and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). From 2005 to 2018, hospitalized CLD patients increased from 71,214 to 122,810 (AAPC, 4.37%; 95% CI, 3.87%-4.88%), and deaths from 11,455 to 24,560 (6.02%; 4.20%-7.86%). ASHPR increased from 275.12 to 377.88 per 100,000, and ASMR from 45.53 to 74.77. Hospitalizations and charges increased from 116,482 to 185,268 and $9.63 billion to $18.63 billion, while in-hospital mortality declined (AAPC, -7.02%; 95% CI, -8.72%-5.30%). MASLD- and ALD-related hospitalizations increased, whereas HBV- and HCV-related hospitalizations declined. Men had higher hospitalization and mortality rates, particularly for ALD. Hispanic populations had the fastest-rising burden, driven by MASLD; HBV burden was concentrated among non-Hispanic Asian populations, whereas overall CLD and ALD-related mortality were highest among non-Hispanic White populations. Findings highlight the need for targeted prevention and screening, early management of metabolic and alcohol-related risk factors, and equitable access to liver care. No funding.

items.title: TMEM121 aggravates acetaminophen-induced pyroptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma cells by activating the NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD pathway.
items.abstract: Acetaminophen (APAP) is a widely used analgesic and antipyretic drug, but overdose causes severe acute liver injury. TMEM121 is an evolutionarily conserved transmembrane protein with high expression in liver tissue, yet its role in liver injury remains unknown. To investigate the function and molecular mechanism of the TMEM121 gene in APAP-induced injury in hepatoma carcinoma cells, we comprehensively employed three analytical approaches: bioinformatics prediction, cellular functional assays, and detection of key molecules in the pyroptosis pathway. Firstly, molecular docking analysis revealed that TMEM121 protein can directly bind to APAP. Analysis of the GSE104601 dataset and cellular experiments confirmed that APAP negatively regulates TMEM121 gene expression. Upon APAP stimulation, TMEM121 overexpression increased the sensitivity of Huh7 cells to APAP and reversed the promoting effects of TMEM121 on cell proliferation and migration observed under unstimulated conditions. Mechanistically, Western blotting and ELISA were used to assess key components of the pyroptosis pathway. The results demonstrated that, upon APAP stimulation, TMEM121 overexpression upregulated the expression of NLRP3 and caspase-1, promoted the cleavage of GSDMD to generate the active fragment GSDMD-N, and significantly increased the release of the inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18, thereby exacerbating pyroptosis. Furthermore, the lactate dehydrogenase release assay and transmission electron microscopy observation confirmed that TMEM121 overexpression aggravated APAP-induced cell membrane damage, leading to characteristic morphological features of pyroptosis, including membrane ballooning, rupture, and leakage of cellular contents. In summary, this study reveals that TMEM121 gene acts as a critical regulator of APAP-induced injury in Huh7 cells by activating the NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD signaling pathway and aggravating APAP-induced pyroptosis, providing novel mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic targets for APAP-induced hepatotoxicity. 对乙酰氨基酚(acetaminophen，APAP)是常见的解热镇痛药，但其过量使用可导致严重的药物性肝损伤。人跨膜蛋白121(transmembrane protein121，TMEM121)是一种进化保守的跨膜蛋白，在肝脏组织中有较显著的表达，但其在肝脏损伤中的功能未知。为探讨 TMEM121 基因在APAP诱导的肝癌细胞损伤中的作用及其分子机制，本研究综合运用生物信息学预测、细胞功能实验和焦亡通路关键分子检测等方法进行了分析。首先，通过分子对接分析，发现TMEM121蛋白与APAP存在直接结合能力；GSE104601数据集分析及细胞实验证实，APAP负调控 TMEM121 基因的表达。在APAP刺激下，TMEM121过表达增加了Huh7细胞对APAP的敏感性，且逆转了TMEM121在未受刺激时对细胞增殖与迁移的促进作用。在机制探讨方面，利用蛋白质免疫印迹、ELISA等方法对焦亡通路关键分子进行检测，结果显示在APAP刺激下，TMEM121过表达可上调NLRP3和caspase-1的表达，促进GSDMD发生剪切生成活性片段GSDMD-N，同时显著增加炎症因子IL-1β与IL-18的释放，加剧细胞焦亡的发生。乳酸脱氢酶释放实验及透射电镜观察进一步证实，TMEM121过表达加重了APAP引起的细胞膜损伤，并使细胞呈现细胞膜气泡状凸起、破裂及内容物外溢等典型焦亡形态特征。综上所述，本研究揭示了TMEM121是APAP肝损伤中的一个关键调控因子，通过激活NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD信号通路加剧APAP诱导的肝癌细胞焦亡，为深入解析APAP药物性肝损伤的分子机制提供了新的理论依据和潜在靶点。.

items.title: Characterization of the morphological, immunophenotypical and cytogenetic features of high-grade B-cell lymphoma with 11q aberration.
items.abstract: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with 11q aberration is a rare neoplasm of mature B-cell lineage, and large-scale clinicopathological studies of this disease remain scarce. To bridge this research gap, we conducted a retrospective analysis of HGBCL with 11q aberration, aiming to elucidate its pathogenesis, clinicopathological features and molecular profiles. By reviewing our hospital's case database from 2021 to 2025, we retrospectively screened 92 cases of high-grade or diffuse large B-cell lymphoma that had 11q fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) testing. Among them, 27 cases were confirmed to harbour 11q aberration and were enrolled in the present study. This cohort consisted of 24 males and 3 females with a median age of 61 years (range, 6-85). Eighteen (67%) patients presented with extranodal disease and nine (33%) had nodal disease. The gastrointestinal tract was the most commonly involved extranodal site (13 patients); two of these patients had concurrent lymph node involvement in the head and neck. Fourteen (52%) patients had advanced Ann Arbor stage (III, IV) disease. Eight (30%) patients had a history of immunocompromise including HIV infection, liver or kidney transplantation and other malignant tumours. The bone marrow was negative for lymphoma at initial diagnosis in all 21 patients assessed. Histologically, 20 (74%) cases had Burkitt-like or blastoid morphology and seven (26%) cases showed diffuse large B-cell-like morphology. Most cases (96%, 26/27) had a germinal centre B-cell immunophenotype. c-MYC was positive in all 26 tested cases and BCL2 was negative in 24 of 27 (89%) of cases. Mutational analysis was performed in 14 cases and potential driver mutations were identified in all involving 44 genes. The most frequently affected genes included TP53, IGLL5, DDX3X, BTG2, FOXO1, HIST1H1E and MYC. Following therapy, 24 patients achieved complete remission and disease-free survival. The prognosis was not related to the morphological features, Ann Arbor stage, co-occurrence of MYC aberrations or the chemotherapy regimens. High-grade B-cell lymphoma with 11q aberration may occur across all ages and confers a favourable prognosis. These tumours manifest morphological heterogeneity, and most cases display a Burkitt lymphoma-like immunophenotype characterized by CD10 positivity and BCL2 negativity. The most frequently mutated genes in our cohort are TP53, IGLL5, DDX3X, BTG2, FOXO1, HIST1H1E and MYC.

items.title: Primetime for the Gasdermins Seesaw in Intestinal Homeostasis and Digestive Disorders.
items.abstract: The five pore-forming gasdermins (GSDMs, namely GSDMA-E) are best known for executing pyroptosis, a lytic and highly inflammatory form of programmed cell death. Accumulating evidence over the past decade has unveiled diverse nonlytic functions of GSDMs in digestive homeostasis and disease. GSDMs preserve intestinal barrier integrity and mucosal immunity under physiological conditions, whereas their dysregulated activation fuels tissue injury across a spectrum of digestive diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease, acute intestinal injury, radiation enteritis, acute pancreatitis, and liver disorders. Notably, the functional outcome of GSDM activation is highly context-dependent: the same protein can be either protective or injurious. This duality extends to digestive oncology, where GSDM-mediated pyroptosis can stimulate or suppress antitumor immunity. GSDM-targeted drugs, including GSDMD agonists, GSDMD inhibitors, and GSDME inhibitors, have shown encouraging efficacy in preclinical models, although none have yet reached the clinic. Here, we review the dual roles of GSDMs across the digestive system, outline the mechanistic basis of their form-, cell-, and tissue-specific functions, and discuss the progress and remaining challenges in GSDM-targeted therapy.

items.title: Hepatocyte CBX2 Safeguards Hepatic Lipid Homeostasis by Elevating Ca 2+ -CaMKK2-AMPK Signaling to Counter MASLD.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately one-third of adults and lacks effective pharmacological therapies. Here, we identify Chromobox 2 (CBX2), a Polycomb-associated chromatin regulator, as a previously unrecognized regulator of hepatic lipid homeostasis. CBX2 expression is markedly reduced in hepatocytes from patients with MASLD, multiple mouse models (db/db, ob/ob, HFD, and HFHC), and steatotic hepatocytes in vitro. Hepatocyte-specific CBX2 overexpression ameliorates hepatic steatosis, improves glucose metabolism, and suppresses inflammation, whereas CBX2 deficiency exacerbates these metabolic disturbances. Mechanistically, CBX2 enhances H3K4me3 enrichment at the Orai1 promoter, promoting Orai1 transcription and increasing intracellular Ca 2+ levels. Elevated Ca 2+ activates the CaMKK2-AMPK signaling pathway, leading to ACC phosphorylation, inhibition of de novo lipogenesis (FAS, ACC, and SCD-1), enhancement of fatty acid oxidation (PPARα and CPT-1a), and suppression of NF-κB/JNK-mediated inflammation. Genetic and pharmacological interventions further establish the necessity of this Ca 2+ -CaMKK2-AMPK axis for CBX2-mediated metabolic protection. Collectively, our findings reveal a CBX2-driven metabolic regulatory circuit and highlight CBX2 and its downstream signaling pathway as potential therapeutic targets for MASLD.

items.title: Cannabidiol (CBD) for Pain: A Narrative Review of Evidence to Date.
items.abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD), the principal non-intoxicating phytocannabinoid of Cannabis sativa , is widely marketed and self-administered for pain relief, yet its regulatory status as an analgesic remains unapproved. This review synthesizes preclinical mechanistic data, human pharmacokinetic data, and clinical trial evidence across major pain conditions in order to summarize the current evidence for, or against, efficacy and safety for pain. A synthesis of published information was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, PubMed Central, Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, and other databases, integrating findings from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and pharmacology reviews on CBD (independent of combination products where possible) and pain of any etiology. Preclinical and mechanistic data support plausible physical analgesic pathways for CBD, including receptor modulation, indirect enhancement of endocannabinoid tone via fatty-acid-binding-protein (FABP) inhibition, and anti-inflammatory effects. However, translation to clinical benefit has been inconsistent. In the largest meta-analysis of cannabinoids for pain, cannabinoids reduced chronic pain and improved sleep quality, but effect sizes fell below predefined minimally important clinical differences, and cannabinoids showed no benefit for acute or cancer pain, while increasing non-serious adverse events. CBD randomized trials in knee osteoarthritis, fibromyalgia, and acute low back pain have consistently failed to separate from placebo, whereas smaller/lower-quality trials and observational surveys report subjective benefit. Safety data increasingly point to dose-dependent hepatotoxicity risk. Despite strong biological plausibility and considerable consumer use, current high-quality evidence does not support CBD monotherapy as an effective analgesic across most pain conditions studied to date. Safety monitoring, particularly of liver enzymes at higher doses, is warranted.
